title: WHAT IF YOU WENT BACK TO 2010 WITH $100?

segments.line: But you remember what comes next.
On the nineteenth of June, the biggest bitcoin exchange in the world gets hacked.
For a few minutes, the price drops to one cent.
One cent. That's real.
Your three hundred thousand dollars will be worth one hundred.
Back where you started. You
know it comes back. But you also know what happens after that. And that's the problem.
To get rich from bitcoin, you don't just have to buy it. You have to keep it.
For fourteen years.
In 2014, that same exchange, Mt. Gox, collapses.
About eight hundred and fifty thousand bitcoins vanish.
People who kept their coins there lose everything. That's real.
Then there are the crashes. In 2017 bitcoin hits almost twenty thousand dollars. A year later, it's lost more than eighty percent.
It happens again in 2022.
Every time, the news says bitcoin is dead.
Every time, almost everyone sells.
But the worst danger isn't the crashes. It's you.
A bitcoin is just a secret password.
Lose the password, and the coins are gone. Forever.
In 2013, a man in Wales threw out an old hard drive with eight thousand bitcoins on it.
It's still in a landfill. In
2021, another man said he had two guesses left before his locked drive wipes seven thousand bitcoins.
One study guessed that about one in every five bitcoins is lost forever.
And your password? It's in a file on the family computer. The one
Ellie plays games on. The
one that crashes every Tuesday.
So now you have three problems. Hackers. Crashes. And a little sister with sticky fingers. And
very soon, a fourth problem.
